decisions.rationale: The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying the track starts with a lot of percussion, including drum machines, live drums, a Univox drum machine, and Swedien's statement that he thought it was an SR55.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text identifying John Robinson on drums and stating Michael did all his vocals on Swedien's unpainted, unvarnished, about eight-foot-square drum platform.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying this was the first track recorded for the album and that Paul McCartney came to the studio prepared for the duet.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying Michael Jackson did the wolf howls and that some library material was also present.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying the intro synth was a stock Synclavier patch, the team wanted unique unrecognizable sounds, and Michael loved it and made them keep it.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text identifying Louis Johnson from the Brothers Johnson as the bass player and describing a DI with a UTC transformer producing warm low end.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying the track was written by Steve Porcaro of Toto with John Bettis and that Porcaro played and programmed many synths.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying P.Y.T. used a lot of Minimoog and that Michael Boddicker was the synth programmer there all the time who programmed it.
The declared offsets exactly match retained text saying Rod Temperton wrote the song and that every musical detail was written down or accounted for in Rod's mind when he came to the studio.
